--- title: >- [Table.fmt()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Attach a formatting function to a column. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package/blob/main/tinytab/_table.py#L84-L127){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Table.fmt( column, fn, ) ``` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [column]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column to format. [fn]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable[[Any], str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A function that takes a single value and returns a string. Missing values (`None`) are rendered as empty cells and are never passed to `fn`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new table; the original is not modified. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Format the `price` column as US dollars: ::: {#c8dc0ae1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from tinytab import Table, fmt_currency tbl = Table({"item": ["coffee", "bagel"], "price": [3.5, 2.25]}) tbl.fmt("price", fmt_currency) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
itemprice
coffee$3.50
bagel$2.25
``` ::: ::: Any function that takes a value and returns a string works as a formatter: ::: {#88f15508 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} tbl.fmt("price", lambda x: f"{x:.1f} USD") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
itemprice
coffee3.5 USD
bagel2.2 USD
``` ::: :::
